existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: The copy charge must be an amount that reasonably includes all costs related to reproducing the information, including materials, labor, and overhead.
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: The charge for providing a copy of public information shall be an amount that reasonably includes all costs related to reproducing the public information, including costs of materials, labor, and overhead.
existing_fee_payment_rules.notes: 'reasonably' -> soft-standard; per-item rates are capped by AG rules (TX-0027).

existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: For a request of 50 or fewer pages of paper records, the charge may not include materials, labor, or overhead and is limited to the per-page photocopy charge, unless the pages are in two-or-more unconnected buildings or a remote storage facility.
existing_fee_payment_rules.trigger: Request is for 50 or fewer pages of paper records.
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: If a request is for 50 or fewer pages of paper records, the charge for providing the copy of the public information may not include costs of materials, labor, or overhead, but shall be limited to the charge for each page of the paper record that is photocopied, unless the pages to be photocopied are located in: (1) two or more separate buildings that are not physically connected with each other; or (2) a remote storage facility.
existing_fee_payment_rules.notes: Distinct fee-calc branch for small requests. § 552.261(c) clarifies covered/connected buildings are not 'separate.'

existing_fee_payment_rules.legal_concept: Charges capped by attorney general cost rules
existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: Charges for copies/inspection may not exceed the amounts established by attorney general rule; a non-state governmental body setting its own charges may not exceed the AG-established amounts by more than 25% absent an exemption.
existing_fee_payment_rules.trigger: Body imposes a charge for copies or inspection.
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: The charges for providing copies of public information may not be excessive and may not exceed the actual cost of producing the information ... [a non-state governmental body's charges] may not exceed 25 percent greater than the amount established by the attorney general unless the governmental body requests an exemption.
existing_fee_payment_rules.notes: The concrete per-page/per-hour rate ceilings live in the AG's cost rules at 1 Tex. Admin. Code ch. 70, not in the statute. Source_language assembled from a partial fetch; verify exact wording of § 552.262.

existing_fee_payment_rules.legal_concept: Required written itemized estimate when charge exceeds $40
existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: If a copy charge (or a § 552.271 paper-inspection charge) will exceed $40, the body must give the requestor a written itemized statement detailing all estimated charges (including labor/personnel), notice of any less-costly alternative, and the requestor's response responsibilities.
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: If a request for a copy of public information will result in the imposition of a charge under this subchapter that exceeds $40, or a request to inspect a paper record will result in the imposition of a charge under Section 552.271 that exceeds $40, the governmental body shall provide the requestor with a written itemized statement that details all estimated charges that will be imposed, including any allowable charges for labor or personnel costs.
existing_fee_payment_rules.notes: $40 is a fixed statutory trigger threshold (a state-fixed value the city cannot alter).

existing_fee_payment_rules.legal_concept: Withdrawal for no response to itemized estimate within 10 business days
existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: The request is considered withdrawn if the requestor does not respond in writing within 10 business days after the itemized statement is sent (accepting charges, modifying the request, or filing an overcharge complaint).
existing_fee_payment_rules.trigger: 10 business days elapse after the itemized statement is sent with no written response.
existing_fee_payment_rules.clock_spec: 10 business-days from date the itemized statement is sent
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: A request described by Subsection (a) is considered to have been withdrawn by the requestor if the requestor does not respond in writing to the itemized statement by informing the governmental body within 10 business days after the date the statement is sent to the requestor that: (1) the requestor will accept the estimated charges; (2) the requestor is modifying the request in response to the itemized statement; or (3) the requestor has sent to the attorney general a complaint alleging that the requestor has been overcharged for being provided with a copy of the public information.

existing_fee_payment_rules.legal_concept: Updated itemized statement when charges rise 20% or more
existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: If, before making the copy available, the body determines estimated charges will exceed the itemized statement by 20% or more, it must send a written updated itemized statement; no timely response to the update means the request is withdrawn.
existing_fee_payment_rules.trigger: Estimated charges will exceed the prior itemized statement by 20% or more.
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: If the governmental body later determines, but before it makes the copy or the paper record available, that the estimated charges will exceed the charges detailed in the written itemized statement by 20 percent or more, the governmental body shall send to the requestor a written updated itemized statement that details all estimated charges that will be imposed, including any allowable charges for labor or personnel costs. If the requestor does not respond in writing to the updated estimate in the time and manner described by Subsection (b), the request is considered to have been withdrawn by the requestor.
existing_fee_payment_rules.notes: 20% is a fixed statutory variance threshold. Actual charge cap tied to the (updated) estimate per § 552.2615(d).

existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: A body that sets time limits on uncompensated personnel time must allow at least 36 hours per requestor over a 12-month period and at least 15 hours per requestor in a one-month period before charging for personnel time.
existing_fee_payment_rules.trigger: Body has adopted personnel-time limits under § 552.275.
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: [The yearly time limit] may not be less than 36 hours for a requestor during the 12-month period ... [the monthly time limit] may not be less than 15 hours for a requestor for a one-month period.
existing_fee_payment_rules.notes: Floor: the statutory minimum the city must allow; the city sets the actual limit at or above it. Verbatim phrases quoted from (b); bracketed lead-ins added for readability. Once the limit is met, § 552.275(e) requires a cost estimate within 10 business days.

existing_fee_payment_rules.legal_concept: Waiver or reduction in the public interest
existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: The body must provide a copy without charge or at a reduced charge if it determines waiver/reduction is in the public interest because providing the copy primarily benefits the general public.
existing_fee_payment_rules.trigger: Body determines providing the copy primarily benefits the general public.
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: A governmental body shall provide a copy of public information without charge or at a reduced charge if the governmental body determines that waiver or reduction of the charge is in the public interest because providing the copy of the information primarily benefits the general public.
existing_fee_payment_rules.notes: Duty is triggered by a discretionary public-interest determination.

existing_fee_payment_rules.legal_concept: Waiver when collection cost exceeds the charge
existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: The body may waive the charge if the cost of processing the collection of the charge would exceed the amount of the charge.
existing_fee_payment_rules.trigger: Cost of collecting the charge exceeds the charge itself.
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: If the cost to a governmental body of processing the collection of a charge for providing a copy of public information will exceed the amount of the charge, the governmental body may waive the charge.

existing_fee_payment_rules.legal_concept: Deposit or bond for anticipated costs
existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: The officer may require a deposit or bond for anticipated copy costs once an itemized estimate has been provided and the estimated charge exceeds $100 (body with more than 15 full-time employees) or $50 (fewer than 16 full-time employees).
existing_fee_payment_rules.trigger: Itemized estimate provided and estimated charge exceeds the applicable threshold.
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: An officer for public information or the officer's agent may require a deposit or bond for payment of anticipated costs for the preparation of a copy of public information if: (1) the officer for public information or the officer's agent has provided the requestor with the written itemized statement required under Section 552.2615 ... detailing the estimated charge for providing the copy; and (2) the charge for providing the copy of the public information specifically requested by the requestor is estimated by the governmental body to exceed: (A) $100, if the governmental body has more than 15 full-time employees; or (B) $50, if the governmental body has fewer than 16 full-time employees.
existing_fee_payment_rules.notes: Two-tier fixed thresholds tied to full-time-employee count.

existing_fee_payment_rules.legal_concept: Deposit for unpaid amounts from prior requests
existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: The officer may require a deposit or bond for unpaid amounts owed on prior requests if those unpaid amounts exceed $100, and this becomes the sole means of collecting those amounts.
existing_fee_payment_rules.trigger: Requestor has unpaid amounts exceeding $100 from prior requests.
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: An officer for public information or the officer's agent may require a deposit or bond for payment of unpaid amounts owing to the governmental body in relation to previous requests that the requestor has made ... only if those unpaid amounts exceed $100.
existing_fee_payment_rules.notes: Source_language reconstructed from a full-text reproduction summary; verify exact subsection and wording (overdue-balance provision of § 552.263).
